```{r}
# Set working directory

library(Seurat)
library(ggpubr)
library(ggplot2)
library(ezRun)
library(SCpubr)
library(qs2)
library(remotes)
library(scales)
library(scProportionTest)  # provides sc_utils(), permutation_test(), permutation_plot()


```

```{r}
seurat_path <- file.path("data", "scMulti_HDM.qs2")  # processed single-cell object — see README (Data availability) for access
scData <- qs_read(seurat_path, nthreads = 8)

# Set the assay to RNA
DefaultAssay(scData) <- "RNA"
```

```{r}
scData$cellType <- dplyr::recode(
  scData$cellType,
  "Myocytes" = "dSMCs2",
  "dSMCs1"  = "dSMCs1",
  "dSMCs2" = "dSMCs2",
  "dSMCs3"  = "dSMCs3"
)

Idents(scData) <- "cellType"
table(scData@meta.data$cellType)
```


```{r}
# Figure S2C
library(Seurat)
library(ggplot2)

# STEP 1: Color palette without yellow
cols_1 <- c("#8DD3C7", "#E78AC3", "#BEBADA", "#FB8072", 
           "#80B1D3", "#FDB462", "#B3DE69", "#FCCDE5", 
           "#D9D9D9", "#BC80BD", "#CCEBC5", "#8DA0CB")

# STEP 2: Base plot (with split.by added)
p <- DimPlot(
  object = scData,            
  reduction = "umap",         
  label = TRUE,               
  label.size = 5,              # Labels can get too large when split, so size reduced a bit
  # CHANGED HERE: column name in metadata should be "condition"
  pt.size = 0.2,              
  raster = FALSE,             
  cols = cols_1 
)

# STEP 3: Transparency
p$layers[[1]]$aes_params$alpha <- 0.7

# STEP 4: AXIS AND FONT SETTINGS
p + ggtitle("Annotated UMAP") +
  theme(
    # --- GENERAL FONT ---
    text = element_text(family = "sans"), 
    
    # --- AXIS TITLES ---
    axis.title = element_text(size = 18, face = "bold", color = "black"),
    
    # --- AXIS TEXT ---
    axis.text = element_text(size = 15, face = "plain", color = "black"),
    
    # --- PLOT TITLE ---
    plot.title = element_text(size = 20, face = "bold", hjust = 0.5),
    
    # --- LEGEND ---
    legend.text = element_text(size = 15),
    legend.title = element_text(size = 15, face = "bold"),
    
    # --- STRIP (Condition labels above each panel) ---
    strip.text = element_text(size = 18, face = "bold") 
  )
```

## Plotting Cellcounts as barplots


```{r}
# Figure 2D
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
library(scales) # required for percent_format

# 1. First define our color palette (the 12-color set you wanted)
custom_colors_revised <- c(
  "#8DD3C7", "#E78AC3", "#BEBADA", "#FB8072", 
  "#80B1D3", "#FDB462", "#B3DE69", "#FCCDE5", 
  "#D9D9D9", "#BC80BD", "#CCEBC5", "#8DA0CB"
)

# 2. Function definition (stays the same)
cell_counts_by_condition <- function(seurat_obj, celltype_col, condition_col = "condition") {
  md <- seurat_obj@meta.data
  stopifnot(celltype_col %in% colnames(md), condition_col %in% colnames(md))
  
  as.data.frame(table(
      cellType  = md[[celltype_col]],
      condition = md[[condition_col]]
    ), stringsAsFactors = FALSE) |>
    dplyr::rename(n_cells = Freq)
}

# 3. Prepare the data
cell_counts <- cell_counts_by_condition(
  seurat_obj = scData,
  celltype_col = "cellType", # This should be the column name in your data
  condition_col = "condition"
)

# Order by cell counts (automatic)
celltype_levels <- cell_counts %>%
  group_by(cellType) %>%
  summarise(total_cells = sum(n_cells), .groups = "drop") %>%
  arrange(desc(total_cells)) %>%
  pull(cellType)

cell_counts <- cell_counts %>%
  mutate(cellType = factor(cellType, levels = celltype_levels))

# --- PLOT 1: TOTAL CELL COUNTS ---
p_total <- ggplot(cell_counts, aes(x = condition, y = n_cells, fill = cellType)) +
  geom_col(position = position_dodge(width = 0.9), width = 0.8, color = "black") +
  
  # ADDING THE COLORS HERE
  scale_fill_manual(values = custom_colors_revised) + 
  
  labs(x = "Condition", y = "Number of cells", fill = "Cell type") +
  theme_classic() +
  theme(
    text = element_text(color = "black"),
    axis.text = element_text(color = "black")
  )

# --- SECOND PART: PROPORTIONAL (PERCENTAGE) PLOT ---
cell_counts_rel <- cell_counts %>%
  group_by(condition) %>%
  mutate(n_total = sum(n_cells), pct = n_cells / n_total) %>%
  ungroup()

# Manual ordering (the list from your code)
# Note: if your data has a cell type not in this list, it will become NA, so watch out.
my_levels <- c("Pax7_PGs1", "Pax7_PGs2", "Pax7_PGs3", "Prolif_MB", 
               "Diff_MB", "dSMCs1", "dSMCs2", "dSMCs3", "dSMCs4", 
               "FAPs1", "FAPs2")

# Only factorize the ones actually present in the data (to avoid errors)
cell_counts_rel$cellType <- factor(cell_counts_rel$cellType, levels = my_levels)

# --- PLOT 2: PERCENTAGE DISTRIBUTION ---
p_rel <- ggplot(cell_counts_rel, aes(x = condition, y = pct, fill = cellType)) +
  geom_col(color = "black") + # Black border line
  
  scale_y_continuous(labels = percent_format(accuracy = 1)) +
  
  # ADDING THE COLORS HERE TOO
  scale_fill_manual(values = custom_colors_revised) +
  
  labs(x = "Condition", y = "Cell type composition", fill = "Cell type") +
  theme_classic() +
  theme(
    text = element_text(color = "black"),
    axis.text = element_text(color = "black")
  )

# Render both plots
print(p_total)
print(p_rel)
```



```{r calculating foldchanges for celltype abundances between HDM and HDM FR condition}

prop_test <- sc_utils(scData)

prop_test <- permutation_test(
	prop_test, cluster_identity = "cellType",
	sample_1 = "HDM_FR", sample_2 = "HDM",
	sample_identity = "condition"
)



p1 <- permutation_plot(prop_test, 
                       FDR_threshold = 0.05,
                       log2FD_threshold = log2(1.45))



p1
```


```{r making a prettier plot}
# Figure S2D
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)

# 1. Define the specific populations you want to keep
# Replace these with the exact names of your clusters
my_clusters <- c("Pax7_PGs1","Pax7_PGs2","Pax7_PGs3","Prolif_MB", "Diff_MB", "dSMCs1","dSMCs2","dSMCs3","FAPs1","FAPs2") 

df_plot <- prop_test@results$permutation %>%
  
  # --- FILTER STEP ---
  # Keep only the rows where the cluster name is in your list
  filter(clusters %in% my_clusters) %>%
  
  # --- INVERT COMPARISON STEP ---
  # To switch from A vs B to B vs A:
  # 1. Multiply Log2FD by -1
  # 2. Multiply CIs by -1 and SWAP them (High becomes Low, Low becomes High)
  mutate(
    obs_log2FD = -obs_log2FD,
    new_CI_low = -boot_CI_97.5, 
    new_CI_high = -boot_CI_2.5
  ) %>%
  
  # --- RECALCULATE SIGNIFICANCE ---
  # Re-run logic on the NEW obs_log2FD values
  mutate(sig_dir = case_when(
    FDR < 0.05 & obs_log2FD < -0.5 ~ "Down",
    FDR < 0.05 & obs_log2FD > 0.5 ~ "Up",
    TRUE ~ "n.s."
  )) %>%
  
  # Re-order the factor based on the new values so the plot looks organized
  mutate(clusters = factor(clusters,
                           levels = clusters[order(obs_log2FD, decreasing = TRUE)]))


# --- PLOTTING ---
p <- ggplot(df_plot,
            aes(x = obs_log2FD, y = clusters, color = sig_dir)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0,
             linewidth = 0.6,
             color = "black") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = c(-0.5, 0.5),
             linetype = "dashed",
             linewidth = 0.5,
             color = "grey60") +
  
  # Note: Use the NEW inverted CI columns here
  geom_errorbarh(aes(xmin = new_CI_low, xmax = new_CI_high),
                 height = 0.2,
                 linewidth = 0.7) +
  
  geom_point(size = 3) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("Down" = "#0072B2",
                                "Up"   = "#B71C1C",
                                "n.s." = "grey75"),
                     breaks = c("Down", "Up", "n.s."),
                     labels = c("Down (FDR < 0.05, log2FD < -0.5)",
                                "Up (FDR < 0.05, log2FD > 0.5)",
                                "n.s. (FDR ≥ 0.05, & -0.5 < FDR < 0.5)")) +
  
  # Update the label to reflect the new direction (I swapped the order below)
  labs(x = "log2 fold difference (HDM vs HDM_FR)", 
       y = NULL,
       color = "Significance thresholds") +
  theme_classic(base_size = 12) +
  theme(legend.position = "right",
        legend.title = element_text(size = 10),
        legend.text = element_text(size = 9))

p


```

```{r}
fast_maturation_genes_SHORT <- c("SIX1", "MYH1", "MYH2", "MYL1", "MYOM2",
                                 "TRDN", "TNNI2", "TNNC2", "ENO3", "CKM", "LDHA")

  scData,
  features = fast_maturation_genes_SHORT,
  idents = selected_clusters,  # <-- Cluster selection happens here
  pt.size = 0,
  stack = TRUE,
  flip = TRUE,
  cols = c("#000000", "#667CFF"),
  split.by = "condition"
)

p + 
  theme(
    # Y axis (flip = TRUE → gene names go here)
    axis.text.y  = element_text(size = 10, face = "bold"),
    axis.title.y = element_text(size = 20),
    
    # X axis (expression scale)
    axis.text.x  = element_text(size = 14),
    axis.title.x = element_text(size = 18),
    
    # General
    legend.text  = element_text(size = 16),
    legend.title = element_text(size = 18)
  )
```

```{r}
#FİGURE 2L
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
library(Seurat)

# ---------------------------------------------------------
# EXISTING FUNCTION (Single or Manual Split)
# ---------------------------------------------------------

plot_and_save_features <- function(seurat_obj, features_list, split_col = NULL, pt_size = 4) {
  
  for (gene in features_list) {
    
    # 1. Plot Creation
    p <- FeaturePlot(seurat_obj, 
                     features = gene, 
                     reduction = "umap", 
                     split.by = split_col,
                     order = TRUE,
                     pt.size = pt_size, # Fixed: uses the function argument now
                     cols= c("lightgray","#667CFF")) 
    
    # 2. Update Theme
    p <- p + theme(
      plot.title = element_text(size = 25, face = "bold"),
      axis.title = element_text(size = 25),
      axis.text = element_text(size = 25),
      legend.text = element_text(size = 25),
      legend.title = element_text(size = 25)
    )
    
    # 3. File Name
    suffix <- ifelse(is.null(split_col), "", paste0("_", split_col))
    file_name <- paste0(gene, "_UMAP", suffix, ".pdf")
    
    # 4. Save (Standard Size)
    ggsave(filename = file_name, plot = p, width = 6, height = 5, dpi = 300)
    
    # 5. Print and Message
    print(p)
    message(paste("Saved:", file_name))
  }
}

# ---------------------------------------------------------
# NEW FUNCTION: Optimized for Splitting Conditions
# ---------------------------------------------------------

plot_split_features <- function(seurat_obj, features_list, split_col, pt_size = 1) {
  
  # Check if the split column exists
  if (!split_col %in% colnames(seurat_obj@meta.data)) {
    stop(paste("Column", split_col, "not found in metadata!"))
  }
  
  # Calculate dynamic width: 6 inches per condition (prevents squishing)
  num_conditions <- length(unique(seurat_obj@meta.data[[split_col]]))
  dynamic_width <- 6 * num_conditions
  
  for (gene in features_list) {
    
    # 1. Plot Creation (Split forced)
    p <- FeaturePlot(seurat_obj, 
                     features = gene, 
                     reduction = "umap", 
                     split.by = split_col,
                     order = TRUE,
                     pt.size = pt_size,
                     cols= c("lightgray","#667CFF")) 
    
    # 2. Update Theme
    p <- p + theme(
      plot.title = element_text(size = 25, face = "bold"),
      axis.title = element_text(size = 25),
      axis.text = element_text(size = 25),
      legend.text = element_text(size = 25),
      legend.title = element_text(size = 25)
    )
    
    # 3. File Name (Includes 'SPLIT' to distinguish files)
    file_name <- paste0(gene, "_UMAP_SPLIT_by_", split_col, ".pdf")
    
    # 4. Save (Using Dynamic Width)
    ggsave(filename = file_name, plot = p, width = dynamic_width, height = 5, dpi = 300)
    
    # 5. Print and Message
    print(p)
    message(paste("Saved Split Plot:", file_name, "(Width:", dynamic_width, ")"))
  }
}
```
